questions.q: $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{10} \left( \dfrac{528}{n(n+1)(n+2)} \right)$ is equal to:
questions.question: $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{10} \left( \dfrac{528}{n(n+1)(n+2)} \right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $T_n = \dfrac{528}{n(n+1)(n+2)}$

$T_n = \dfrac{528}{2} \left( \dfrac{(n+2) - n}{n(n+1)(n+2)} \right)$

$T_n = 264 \left( \dfrac{1}{n(n+1)} - \dfrac{1}{(n+1)(n+2)} \right)$

The sum of the first $10$ terms is given by:

$S_{10} = \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n = 264 \displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{10} \left( \dfrac{1}{n(n+1)} - \dfrac{1}{(n+1)(n+2)} \right)$

This is a telescoping series, so most terms cancel out:

$S_{10} = 264 \left( \left( \dfrac{1}{1 \cdot 2} - \dfrac{1}{2 \cdot 3} \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{2 \cdot 3} - \dfrac{1}{3 \cdot 4} \right) + \dots + \left( \dfrac{1}{10 \cdot 11} - \dfrac{1}{11 \cdot 12} \right) \right)$

$S_{10} = 264 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{11 \cdot 12} \right)$

$S_{10} = 264 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{132} \right)$

$S_{10} = 264 \left( \dfrac{66 - 1}{132} \right)$

$S_{10} = 264 \times \dfrac{65}{132}$

$S_{10} = 2 \times 65 = 130$

Answer: $130$

questions.q: If the sum of the first $10$ terms of the series $\dfrac{1}{1 + 1^4 \times 4} + \dfrac{2}{1 + 2^4 \times 4} + \dfrac{3}{1 + 3^4 \times 4} + \dfrac{4}{1 + 4^4 \times 4} + \ldots$ is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, then $m + n$ is equal to :
questions.question: If the sum of the first $10$ terms of the series $\dfrac{1}{1 + 1^4 \times 4} + \dfrac{2}{1 + 2^4 \times 4} + \dfrac{3}{1 + 3^4 \times 4} + \dfrac{4}{1 + 4^4 \times 4} + \ldots$ is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, then $m + n$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
The general term of the series is $T_r = \dfrac{r}{1 + 4r^4}$.

Factorizing the denominator:

$1 + 4r^4 = (1 + 2r^2)^2 - 4r^2 = (2r^2 - 2r + 1)(2r^2 + 2r + 1)$

Thus, $T_r = \dfrac{r}{(2r^2 - 2r + 1)(2r^2 + 2r + 1)}$

Multiplying and dividing by $4$:

$T_r = \dfrac{1}{4} \left[ \dfrac{4r}{(2r^2 - 2r + 1)(2r^2 + 2r + 1)} \right]$

$T_r = \dfrac{1}{4} \left[ \dfrac{1}{2r^2 - 2r + 1} - \dfrac{1}{2r^2 + 2r + 1} \right]$

The sum of the first $10$ terms is:

$S_{10} = \sum_{r=1}^{10} T_r = \dfrac{1}{4} \sum_{r=1}^{10} \left( \dfrac{1}{2r^2 - 2r + 1} - \dfrac{1}{2(r+1)^2 - 2(r+1) + 1} \right)$

This is a telescoping series, so all intermediate terms cancel out:

$S_{10} = \dfrac{1}{4} \left[ \left( \dfrac{1}{1} - \dfrac{1}{5} \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{13} \right) + \ldots + \left( \dfrac{1}{2(10)^2 - 2(10) + 1} - \dfrac{1}{2(10)^2 + 2(10) + 1} \right) \right]$

$S_{10} = \dfrac{1}{4} \left[ 1 - \dfrac{1}{221} \right] = \dfrac{1}{4} \left( \dfrac{220}{221} \right) = \dfrac{55}{221}$

Given $S_{10} = \dfrac{m}{n}$ and $\gcd(m, n) = 1$.

Here, $m = 55$ and $n = 221$. Since $55 = 5 \times 11$ and $221 = 13 \times 17$, $\gcd(55, 221) = 1$.

Therefore, $m + n = 55 + 221 = 276$.

Answer: $276$

questions.question: If $\frac{1}{\sqrt{1}+\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}}+\ldots+\frac{1}{\sqrt{99}+\sqrt{100}}=m$ and $\frac{1}{1 \cdot 2}+\frac{1}{2 \cdot 3}+\ldots+\frac{1}{99 \cdot 100}=n$, then the point $(\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n})$ lies on the line
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{1}+\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}}+\ldots+\frac{1}{\sqrt{99}+\sqrt{100}}=\mathrm{m} \\ & \frac{\sqrt{1}-\sqrt{2}}{-1}+\frac{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{3}}{-1} \ldots \frac{\sqrt{99}-\sqrt{100}}{-1}=\mathrm{m}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{100}-1=\mathrm{m} \Rightarrow \mathrm{m}=9 \\
& \frac{1}{1 \cdot 2}+\frac{1}{2 \cdot 3}+\ldots \frac{1}{99 \cdot 100}=\mathrm{n} \\
& \frac{1}{1}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3} \ldots \frac{1}{99}-\frac{1}{100}=\mathrm{n} \\
& 1-\frac{1}{100}=\mathrm{n} \\
& \frac{99}{100}=\mathrm{n} \\
& (\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n})=\left(9, \frac{99}{100}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 11(9)-100\left(\frac{99}{100}\right) \\
& =99-99=0
\end{aligned}$
Ans.$11 x-100 y=0$

questions.solution:
$\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{20}\dfrac{1}{{a}_{n}{a}_{n + 1}} = \dfrac{4}{9}$ $\text{[let common difference of}\leftAPisd = {a}_{n + 1} - {a}_{n}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{d}\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{20}\left(\dfrac{1}{an} - \dfrac{1}{an + 1}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{1}{d}\left[\left(\dfrac{1}{a1} - \dfrac{1}{a2}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{a3}\right) + \ldots . \left(\dfrac{1}{a20} - \dfrac{1}{a21}\right)\right] = \dfrac{4}{9}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{d}\left(\dfrac{{a}_{21} - {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1} \cdot {a}_{21}}\right) = \dfrac{4}{9} ⇒ \dfrac{20d}{d\left({a}_{1}{a}_{21}\right)} = \dfrac{4}{9} ⇒ {a}_{1}{a}_{21} = 45$

${a}_{1}\left({a}_{1} + 20d\right) = 45 . . . ( 1 )$

Now sum of first $21$ terms$= \dfrac{21}{2}\left(2{a}_{1} + 20d\right) = 189 ⇒ {a}_{1} + 10d = 9 . . . ( 2 )$

by using equation $( 1 )$ and $( 2 )$ we get ${a}_{1} = 3, d = \dfrac{3}{5}$ otherwise ${a}_{1} = 15, d = - \dfrac{3}{5}$

So, ${a}_{6}{a}_{16} = \left({a}_{1} + 5d\right)\left({a}_{1 +} + 15d\right) = 72$

questions.question: Let for $n = 1, 2, \ldots \ldots , 50, {S}_{n}$ be the sum of the infinite geometric progression whose first term is ${n}^{2}$ and whose common ratio is $\dfrac{1}{\left(n + 1\right)2}$. Then the value of $\dfrac{1}{26} + \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({S}_{n} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $a = {n}^{2}, r = \dfrac{1}{\left(n + 1\right)2}$

${S}_{n} = \dfrac{n2}{1 - \dfrac{1}{\left(n + 1\right)2}} = \dfrac{{n}^{2}\left(n + 1\right)2}{n\left(n + 2\right)}$

$= \dfrac{n\left[n\left(n + 2\right) + 1\right]}{n + 2} = {n}^{2} + \dfrac{n}{n + 2}$

$= {n}^{2} + \dfrac{n + 2 - 2}{n + 2}$ $= {n}^{2} + 1 - \dfrac{2}{n + 2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, $\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({S}_{n} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right)$

From equation $\left(i\right)$,

$= \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({n}^{2} + 1 - \dfrac{2}{n + 2} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({n}^{2} - n\right) + 2\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left(\dfrac{1}{n + 1} - \dfrac{1}{n + 2}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}{n}^{2} - \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}n + 2\left[\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) + ⋯ + \left(\dfrac{1}{51} - \dfrac{1}{52}\right)\right]$

$= \dfrac{50\left(51\right)\left(101\right)}{6} - \dfrac{50\left(51\right)}{2} + 2\left[\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{52}\right]$

$= \left(25\right)\left(17\right)\left(101\right) - 25\left(51\right) + \left(\dfrac{50}{52}\right)$

$= 25\left(1717 - 51\right) + \dfrac{50}{52}$ $= 25\left(1666\right) + \dfrac{25}{26}$

$= 41650 + \dfrac{25}{26}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{26} + \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({S}_{n} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right) = 41650 + 1 = 41651$

questions.question: The sum of the series $\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{∞}\dfrac{{n}^{2} + 6n + 10}{\left(2n + 1\right) !}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
${T}_{n} = \dfrac{{n}^{2} + 6n + 10}{\left(2n + 1\right) !} = \dfrac{4{n}^{2} + 24n + 40}{4 . \left(2n + 1\right) !}$

$= \dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right)2 + 20n + 39}{4 . \left(2n + 1\right) !}$

$= \dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right)2 + \left(2n + 1\right) . 10 + 29}{4\left(2n + 1\right) !}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right)2}{\left(2n + 1\right)\left(2n\right) !} + \dfrac{\left(2n + 1\right)10}{\left(2n + 1\right)\left(2n\right) !} + \dfrac{29}{\left(2n + 1\right) !}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{2n + 1}{\left(2n\right) !} + \dfrac{10}{\left(2n\right) !} + \dfrac{29}{\left(2n + 1\right) !}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{1}{\left(2n - 1\right) !} + \dfrac{11}{\left(2n\right) !} + \dfrac{29}{2n + 1 !}\right]$

${S}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{1 !} + \dfrac{1}{3 !} + \dfrac{1}{5 !} + \ldots = \dfrac{e - \dfrac{1}{e}}{2}$

${S}_{2} = 11\left[\dfrac{1}{2 !} + \dfrac{1}{4 !} + \dfrac{1}{6 !} + \ldots\right] = 11\left[\lefte + \dfrac{1}{e} - 2\right]2\right]$

${S}_{3} = 29\left[\dfrac{1}{3 !} + \dfrac{1}{5 !} + \dfrac{1}{7 !} + \ldots\right] = 29\left[\dfrac{e - \dfrac{1}{e} - 2}{2}\right]$

Now, $S = \dfrac{1}{4}\left[{S}_{1} + {S}_{2} + {S}_{3}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{e}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2e} + \dfrac{11e}{2} + \dfrac{11}{2e} + \dfrac{29e}{2} - \dfrac{29}{2e} - 4\right]$

$= \dfrac{41e}{8} - \dfrac{19}{8e} - 10$

questions.question: If $1+\frac{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}{2 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{5-2 \sqrt{6}}{18}+\frac{9 \sqrt{3}-11 \sqrt{2}}{36 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{49-20 \sqrt{6}}{180}+\ldots$ upto $\infty=2+\left(\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}+1\right) \log _e\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)$, where $\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{b}$ are integers with $\operatorname{gcd}(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b})=1$, then $11 \mathrm{a}+18 \mathrm{~b}$ is equal to ______
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & S=1+\frac{x}{2 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{x^2}{18}+\frac{x^3}{36 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{x^4}{180}+\ldots \infty \\ & \text { Put } \frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}=t, \text { where } x=\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2} \\ & S=1+\frac{t}{2}+\frac{t^2}{6}+\frac{t^3}{12}+\frac{t^4}{20}+\ldots \\ & S=1+t\left(1-\frac{1}{2}\right)+t^2\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right)+t^3\left(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}\right)+t^4\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}\right) \\ & S=\left(1+t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^3}{3}+\frac{t^3}{4}+\ldots\right)-\left(\frac{t}{2}+\frac{t^2}{3}+\frac{t^3}{4}+\frac{t^4}{5}+\ldots\right) \\ & S=\left(t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\ldots\right)-\frac{1}{t}\left(t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^3}{3}+\ldots\right)+2 \\ & S=2+\left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right)(-\log (1-t))=\left(\frac{1}{t}-1\right) \log (1-t)+2 \\ & S=2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}-1\right) \log \left(1-\frac{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \\ & S=2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}\right) \log e \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & S=2+\frac{(\sqrt{6}+2)}{2} \log e \frac{2}{3}=2+\left(\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}+1\right) \log e \frac{2}{3} \\ & a=2, b=3 \\ & 11 a+18 b=11 \times 2+18 \times 3=76\end{aligned}$

questions.question: Let $f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}k \cdot {x}^{k}, x \in \mathbb{R}$, if $2f\left(2\right) + {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = 119\left(2\right)n + 1$ then $n$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}k \cdot {x}^{k}, x \in \mathbb{R}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + 2{x}^{2} + 3{x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots \ldots + 10{x}^{10}$

Now let $S = x + 2{x}^{2} + 3{x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots \ldots + 10{x}^{10}$

So, $S \cdot x = {x}^{2} + 2{x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots + 9{x}^{10} + 10{x}^{11}$

Now subtracting above equations we get,

$S\left(1 - x\right) = x + {x}^{2} + {x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots + {x}^{10} - 10{x}^{11}$

$⇒ S\left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{x\left(1 - {x}^{10}\right)}{1 - x} - 10{x}^{11}$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{x\left(1 - {x}^{10}\right)}{\left(1 - x\right)2} - 10{x}^{11}\left(1 - x\right) = f\left(x\right)$

Now finding, $f\left(2\right) = 2\left(1 - {2}^{10}\right) + 10 \cdot {2}^{11}$

$⇒ f\left(2\right) = 2 + 18 \cdot {2}^{10}$

Now finding ${f}^{'}\left(x\right)$ we get,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 10{x}^{11}}{\left(1 - x\right)2} - \dfrac{110{x}^{10}}{1 - x} - \dfrac{10{x}^{10}}{\left(1 - x\right)2} + \dfrac{2x\left(1 - {x}^{10}\right)}{\left(1 - x\right)3} + \dfrac{1 - {x}^{10}}{\left(1 - x\right)2}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = \dfrac{- 10 \cdot {2}^{11}}{\left(1 - 2\right)2} - \dfrac{110 \cdot {2}^{10}}{1 - 2} - \dfrac{10 \cdot {2}^{10}}{\left(1 - 2\right)2} + \dfrac{2 \cdot 2 \cdot \left(1 - {2}^{10}\right)}{\left(1 - 2\right)3} + \dfrac{1 - {2}^{10}}{\left(1 - 2\right)2}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = - 10 \cdot {2}^{11} + 110 \cdot {2}^{10} - 10 \cdot {2}^{10} - 4\left(1 - {2}^{10}\right) + 1 - {2}^{10}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = 83 \cdot {2}^{10} - 3$

$2f ( 2 ) + {f}^{'} ( 2 ) = 2\left(2 + 18 \cdot {2}^{10}\right) + 83 \cdot {2}^{10} - 3 = 119 ( 2{)}^{10} + 1$

$∴ n = 10$

questions.q: Let $a_{1}=1$ and for $n \geqslant 1, a_{n+1}=\frac{1}{2} a_{n}+\frac{n^{2}-2 n-1}{n^{2}(n+1)^{2}}$. Then $\left|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_{n}-\frac{2}{n^{2}}\right)\right|$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.question: Let $a_{1}=1$ and for $n \geqslant 1, a_{n+1}=\frac{1}{2} a_{n}+\frac{n^{2}-2 n-1}{n^{2}(n+1)^{2}}$. Then $\left|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_{n}-\frac{2}{n^{2}}\right)\right|$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
Let $b_n = a_n - \frac{2}{n^2}$.
$b_{n+1} = \frac{1}{2}a_n + \frac{n^2-2n-1}{n^2(n+1)^2} - \frac{2}{(n+1)^2}$.
Simplifying: $b_{n+1} = \frac{1}{2}b_n + \frac{(n+1)^2 + n^2 - 2n - 1 - 2n^2}{n^2(n+1)^2} = \frac{1}{2}b_n$.
So $b_n$ is GP with ratio $\frac{1}{2}$.
$b_1 = 1 - 2 = -1$, so $b_n = -\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1}$.
$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n = -\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2}} = -2$.
$\left|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_n - \frac{2}{n^2}\right)\right| = 2$.
